title: Scheduler overview
summary: Build each week by setting day metadata first, then assigning staff blocks and clearing violations.
howTo: Pick the school and week in the top banner.
Set enrollment, schedule type, and field trip details for each open day.
Enter clock-in and clock-out blocks per staff member. Multiple non-contiguous blocks are allowed.
Open Violation Navigator and resolve all critical items before publishing.
Use the Audit Log to undo or redo recent edits if needed.
examples: Scenario: Monday enrollment is 32 with a 1:10 ratio. Enter the enrollment in the day metadata, then assign at least 4 adults for each active segment so the ratio violation clears.
Scenario: A staff member works a split shift. Add two separate blocks in the same row (7:00 AM–10:30 AM and 2:00 PM–5:00 PM) so the timeline reflects the gap and avoids overlap warnings.

title: Schedule grid
summary: The grid combines day metadata and employee time blocks in one place.
howTo: For each day column, confirm schedule type, enrollment, and field trip values.
Use Add block in a staff row to create a new clock-in/clock-out block.
Click an existing block to edit or delete it.
Review operating hours and the field trip window under the day metadata.
If a red warning appears, adjust times or staffing until the warning clears.
examples: Scenario: A part-time employee works Tuesday morning and afternoon. Use Add block twice to capture 8:00 AM–11:00 AM and 1:00 PM–4:30 PM so the gap is visible and schedule coverage is accurate.
Scenario: Wednesday is marked closed in School settings. The day column stays read-only, so remove any blocks and rely on the closed-day indicator instead of adjusting staff times.

title: Auto-schedule
summary: Auto-schedule can generate a full schedule or improve the existing one.
howTo: Click Auto in the top banner.
If metadata is missing, fill the required day fields first.
Choose whether to replace existing assignments or keep and improve them.
Review remaining violations after the run.
examples: Scenario: You are starting a new week with no assignments. Choose Replace to generate a full draft schedule from ratios and availability.
Scenario: You already adjusted Tuesday manually. Choose Keep to fill remaining gaps without overwriting those edits.

title: Violation navigator
summary: Violations show compliance gaps and link directly to affected schedule blocks.
howTo: Open Violation Navigator from the top banner.
Sort through critical items first.
Use Focus Segment to jump to the exact block or day column.
Make edits in the grid and confirm the violation count decreases automatically.
Ratio issues include the affected time window in the message.
examples: Scenario: A ratio staffing gap appears from 9:00 AM–11:00 AM. Add another qualified staff block during that window or correct the enrollment count until the warning disappears.
Scenario: Two blocks overlap for the same employee. Shorten or move one block so the start and end times no longer collide.

title: Guided status tracker
summary: The tracker enforces Prepare → Assign → Review → Publish and highlights blockers.
howTo: Complete day metadata before assigning staff.
Resolve violations to clear the Review step.
Publish becomes available once all blockers are cleared.
examples: Scenario: Enrollment is missing for Thursday. The Prepare step stays in progress until you enter the count in day metadata.
Scenario: A ratio violation remains on Friday afternoon. The Review step stays blocked until the staffing level meets the required ratio.

title: Publish and exports
summary: Publish locks the week status and exports provide audit-ready records.
howTo: Clear all violations before publishing.
Use the publish action once the tracker shows Review complete.
Export PDF/CSV for audit records after publishing.
examples: Scenario: After Publish turns green, export a PDF for district sign-off and archive it with your audit records.
Scenario: A change request comes in after publishing. Reopen the week, fix the issue, clear violations, then publish again.

title: Audit timeline
summary: Audit timeline records key scheduling actions and supports undo/redo.
howTo: Open Audit Log from the top banner.
Review entries to understand what changed and when.
Use Undo/Redo to move through recent schedule edits.
Use note details to verify school/day context.
Undo history persists per week in the browser.
examples: Scenario: A staff block was deleted by mistake. Open Audit Log and choose Undo to restore it.
Scenario: You want to compare two recent edits. Use Undo to view the previous state, then Redo to return to the newer staffing plan.

title: Settings overview
summary: Settings control ratios, operating windows, and staff data used by validations and scheduling.
howTo: Open Settings from the top banner.
Use tabs to edit one area at a time.
Save each tab before switching or closing.
Return to the schedule grid to apply the updated rules.
examples: Scenario: The district introduces a new program day. Add the schedule type first, then select it in the day metadata so ratios are correct.
Scenario: A staff member changes availability. Update their availability in Settings before placing new blocks so Auto Schedule respects the change.

title: School settings
summary: Set school-level policies such as openers/closers, field trip windows, and closed days.
howTo: Edit school name and baseline policy counts.
Set field trip start and end times for ratio windows.
Set required medical delegation and CPR policy flags.
Mark closed days to disable scheduling for those days.
Save school settings before leaving the tab.
examples: Scenario: The building is closed on Saturdays. Mark Saturday as closed so the grid locks that day and removes staffing requirements.
Scenario: CPR compliance is required. Turn on the CPR requirement so anyone without current CPR triggers a violation until updated.

title: Schedule types
summary: Schedule types define the staffing ratio used by each day.
howTo: Add or edit schedule type names.
Set adult:student ratio values for each type.
Use clear descriptions so directors know when to use each type.
Save schedule types and then apply them in the grid.
examples: Scenario: Define a Full Day type at 1:10 and a Half Day type at 1:12. Select the correct type per day so ratios are calculated correctly.
Scenario: The district uses a "Pre-K Extended" program. Create a custom schedule type label so staff know when to use that ratio.

title: Operating hours
summary: Operating hours define open/close windows by schedule type and day set.
howTo: Create operating hour sets and assign days of week.
Prevent overlap for the same schedule type and day.
Use open and close times that match policy and building operations.
Save once overlap warnings are cleared.
examples: Scenario: Regular operating hours are 7:00 AM–5:30 PM Monday through Friday. Create one set and assign those days together.
Scenario: Summer hours run 8:00 AM–4:00 PM Monday through Thursday. Create a separate schedule type so the grid shows the right open/close window.

title: Field trip rules
summary: Field trip types can enforce stricter adult and leader ratios than normal day ratios.
howTo: Add field trip types used by your school.
Set adult ratio and optional leader ratio.
Set leader ratio to 0:0 to disable leader-specific requirements.
Save then choose the field trip type on the schedule grid.
Field trip ratios apply during the configured field trip window.
examples: Scenario: A zoo trip requires 1 adult per 8 students and 1 leader per 20. Configure both ratios, then select the trip on the day metadata.
Scenario: A campus walk only needs adult ratios. Set leader ratio to 0:0 so only adult coverage is enforced during the field trip window.

title: Job titles
summary: Job title flags determine leadership eligibility and open/close requirements.
howTo: Add job titles used by your staff.
Mark titles as leader qualified when applicable.
Enable open/close leader requirement for titles that must supervise those windows.
Save job title changes before assigning staff.
examples: Scenario: Directors must open and close. Mark Director as leader qualified and required for open/close coverage.
Scenario: Assistants should not satisfy leader requirements. Leave leader qualification unchecked so they do not clear leader violations.

title: Employees
summary: Maintain staff records, availability, and time-off windows used by scheduler validations.
howTo: Create or edit employee records and job titles.
Set max hours/day and max hours/week limits.
Configure availability windows for each day and add requested days off.
Save employee changes before scheduling blocks.
examples: Scenario: An employee can work mornings and afternoons on Monday. Add availability blocks for 7:00 AM–11:00 AM and 1:00 PM–5:00 PM.
Scenario: A staff member is on PTO next week. Enter the time-off range so Auto Schedule avoids assigning them.
